thread:
emma-support: FYI customer on Dedicated; their app started throwing ImportError after `pip install redwood-inference[async]` inside a Debian-slim Docker image. They say it works locally but fails in CI. stacktrace pasted below.

alice-cs: opening escalation with the tenant now, customer is @acme-inc. They reported 500s and SDK import failures, blocking rollout. :grimacing:

emma-support: repro steps they provided: 
```
# dockerfile
FROM python:3.11-slim
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir redwood-inference[async]
python -c "import redwood; from redwood import AsyncClient"
```
Error: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
ImportError: cannot import name 'AsyncClient' from 'redwood' (unknown location)
```
They also attached `pip freeze` from the container: `redwood-inference==1.2.0`, `httpx==0.24.0`, `httpcore==0.17.0`, plus `sniffio`, `certifi`, etc.

devex-sam: first guess: sounds like an extras/dependency mismatch. our async wrapper expects httpx with AsyncClient at the expected import path, but httpx v0.24 may have changed internals for our pinned usage. do we ship strict pins in pyproject for extras? :thinking_face:

eng-ml-raj: we don't pin strictly for httpx in the public package right now — we accept >=0.22,<0.25 to be flexible. that range should include 0.24 though. the import name shouldn't vanish; could be that the wheel built on macOS resolved a different optional dependency set and the container got a mismatched httpcore binary. platform marker issues with poetry lockfiles are common.

infra-ops-jen: can you get `pip show httpx` and `python -c "import httpx; print(httpx.__version__, httpx.__file__)"` from within the failing container? also whether it was a sdist vs wheel install matters (linux wheels sometimes fail and fall back to sdist).

emma-support: asked customer for those, they sent back: `httpx 0.24.0 /usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/httpx/__init__.py` and `httpcore 0.17.0` plus note: they built the image on macOS runner and pushed to a linux-based container registry, then pulled into production.

devex-sam: aha — likely poetry lock/platform markers issue. if the lockfile was generated on macOS, the wheel selection for httpcore/httpx may have differed (binary wheels tied to platform) so `pip install` from that lock snapshot can produce a different set on Linux. poetry's lockfile includes markers but people sometimes vend the wrong artefacts. quick workaround: in customer image rebuild the wheel on linux or `pip install --no-binary :all: httpx httpcore` to force sdist compile (not ideal).

eng-ml-raj: short-term patch we can ship: tighten extras in our pyproject so async extra pins a narrower httpx range that we test against (and add an import-time compatibility check with a clear error message recommending exact httpx/httpcore versions). can someone add a small runtime verification like: `if not hasattr(httpx, "AsyncClient"): raise RuntimeError("Incompatible httpx installed (x.y.z); install httpx>=0.23,<0.25 or use redwood-inference[async]==<expected>")`

infra-ops-jen: also ask customer to try `pip install httpx==0.23.3 httpcore==0.13.7` inside the container and re-test. that's the simplest immediate mitigation.

emma-support: customer tried `pip install httpx==0.23.3` and reported import works now. they said CI pipeline still uses `poetry export -f requirements.txt` and installs from that file in the linux runner which produced 0.24 previously.

devex-sam: action items: 1) add runtime compatibility check + improved error; 2) update docs with recommended pinned httpx pairing for async extra; 3) create a short KB for support about poetry lockfiles being platform-specific (export on linux runners). i'll open a PR for 1 & 2.

eng-ml-raj: I'll own 1 & 2. Proposed snippet for pyproject extras to reduce surprise: 
```
[project.optional-dependencies]
async = ["httpx>=0.23.0,<0.24.0"]
```
(not perfect long term, but safer until we test against 0.24). Also add a test matrix entry for httpx 0.23 and 0.24 to catch regressions.

alice-cs: customer accepted the workaround and asked for ETA. can we mark P0 and ETA today for KB + guidance?

devex-sam: will draft KB and post here. tagging @eng-ml-raj for the PR. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy started for branch fix/async-httpx-pin (CI pipelines triggered) :rocket:

eng-ml-raj: PR opened: add runtime check + docs link. will notify when merged.

emma-support: marking tenant 'acme-inc' as notified, closing immediate escalation once PR merged and KB published. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
